title: XM-Sparse: High-Throughput Sparse-Attention LLM Serving over Scale-up Memory Pools
abstract: arXiv:2611.22280v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sparse attention has been increasingly adopted by production LLMs for long-context inference, yet serving systems must still retain the full KV history, making GPU HBM capacity a key limit on serving concurrency. Existing systems offload the KV cache to host memory, but suffer from the limited bandwidth of PCIe and the limited capacity of host memory. Emerging scale-up memory pools (e.g., X-Mem) relieve both limits and open new opportunities for sparse-attention offloading. In this paper, we first conduct an in-depth analysis and reveal that, even with scale-up memory pools, decode throughput remains bounded by HBM capacity, as hot KV buffers and the fully resident indexer key (K-index) cache occupy substantial HBM. Moreover, the two caches exhibit distinct access patterns. Based on these insights, we present XM-Sparse, the first sparse-attention offloading system over scale-up memory expansion. tldr: XM-Sparse是首个基于扩展内存池的稀疏注意力KV缓存卸载系统，通过分析热KV缓冲区与索引器键缓存的不同访问模式并针对性优化，突破了HBM容量对长上下文大模型服务吞吐量的限制。
en_tdlr: XM-Sparse is the first sparse-attention KV-cache offloading system built on scale-up memory pools, which analyzes the distinct access patterns of hot KV buffers and the indexer key cache to overcome HBM capacity limits and achieve high-throughput long-context LLM serving.
